channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Slovakia: PM Robert Fico's NATO Article 5 remarks spark criticism and raise questions about his country's NATO commitment
item.description: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico says he fears war and will do everything he can to keep his country out of one. Critics say his remarks risk weakening NATO, the alliance that was designed to prevent such a war.

item.title: [DW] Famine threatens the Ukrainian town of Oleshky in the southern Kherson region as Russia delays creating a humanitarian evacuation corridor
item.description: Food supplies to the town of Oleshky, in the occupied part of the southern Kherson region, have been cut off since May. Efforts by Kyiv to negotiate the evacuation of civilians with Moscow have been largely unsuccessful.

item.title: [DW] Military aircraft crashes near US air base in Spangdahlem, Germany
item.description: The F-16 pilot was able to safely eject from the plane and was taken to receive medical care. The incident occurred near Spangdahlem Air Base in the German state of Rhineland-Palatinate.

item.title: [DW] 'Swan Song': New book by Princess Diana's brother drops
item.description: A memoir penned by Charles Spencer on his older sister's life has been released, opening old royal wounds nearly three decades after Princess Diana's death.

item.title: [DW] Czech PM Andrej Babis reiterates importance of NATO for his country but rejects calls to increase defense spending
item.description: The US and NATO want Czechia to spend more on defense. Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis says Prague cannot afford faster increases, despite growing warnings about the threat from Russia.

item.title: [DW] 'Pope fever' takes hold as Pope Leo visits France
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is expected to draw huge crowds during his visit to France. As part of his trip, he's also set to address Europe's future and some of the challenges ahead.

item.title: [EU Observer] Chess body FIDE elects Kazakh billionaire, amid Russia’s return to world sports
item.description: The fact a Russia-linked billionaire was elected by 110 votes out of 192 in FIDE was a sad reminder that Putin still had friends outside Europe.

item.title: [DW] European cities seek ways of boosting affordable housing
item.description: In many major urban centers of Europe, the housing shortage has become an explosive social issue. DW looks into various models that have been put in place across the continent.

item.title: [EU Observer] Lithuania moves to lift ban on nuclear weapons as ‘Russians do not attack the strong’
item.description: Lithuania's parliament this week backed a proposal to lift the constitutional ban on the deployment of nuclear weapons and foreign military bases, opening the way for future deployment of nuclear weapons in the country.

item.title: [DW] Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
item.description: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.

item.title: [DW] Russia expected to intensify hybrid war on Europe
item.description: Drone explosions, airspace violations, arson attacks: Poland, Romania, and Moldova are now regularly targeted in Russian attacks against Ukraine. More governments are calling these attacks deliberate acts of aggression.

item.title: [DW] Russian classroom propaganda promotes dying for country, students say
item.description: The Russian government has stepped up its efforts to spread patriotic propaganda in schools. DW spoke to students about textbooks that portray the West as hostile and promote sacrifice for the nation.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘Poor but sexy’ Berlin faces worsening housing crisis and bad fixes, warns German economist
item.description: Over the last decade, Berlin rent has spiked 75 percent to €15.78 per square metre. Economist Alexander Kritikos breaks down the bureaucratic nightmare of building housing in the German capital and warned how the Left's plans to purchase flats from corporate landlords may not yield the desired results.

item.title: [Financial Times] US Treasury threatens crackdown on Wall Street tax-avoidance strategies
item.description: Department limits use of ETFs to avoid taxable gains and says it could target other ‘potentially abusive’ tactics

item.title: [Financial Times] AMD to buy Fei-Fei Li’s AI start-up for $8bn
item.description: World Labs was founded by Stanford University researcher to work on AI models that understand 3D environments

item.title: [Financial Times] Bond sell-off deepens and oil rises as Iran-US deal hopes fade
item.description: Brent crude jumps and 10-year Treasury yield surpasses 5.2% as hopes for US-Iran agreement fade

item.title: [Politico Europe] Block US sanctions on ICC, EU lawmakers tell Commission
item.description: Automatically applying U.S. sanctions "stems from the time when we thought that the Americans were still our friends," said Dutch lawmaker Dirk Gotink.

item.title: [Financial Times] Erdoğan bids to contain fallout from Turkey’s $18bn stock market scandal
item.description: President says those ‘engaged in manipulative schemes’ will be held to account as deputy chair of governing party resigns

item.title: [Financial Times] Netanyahu under pressure over reports he was warned about October 7
item.description: Opposition attacks Israeli premier ahead of election over leaks suggesting Egyptian and Emirati officials alerted him to Hamas threat

item.title: [Politico Europe] Farage is still Labour’s main opponent, says party chair
item.description: Bridget Phillipson also throws her weight behind caps on political party spending limits.

item.title: [EU Observer] From Yemen to Ethiopia and Europe: Everything is connected
item.description: The EU could easily catch cold from a civil war in Ethiopia that has broken out weeks after the capture of the Yemeni coastline by Houthi rebels. These, and other events in the region, are all connected.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Budget : le gouvernement envisage un gel “réversible” des retraites
item.description: L'exécutif travaille à une revalorisation à l’inflation des retraites sous les 1260 euros, et un décret pour déterminer une éventuelle indexation au-delà.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Labour conference: 6 things we learned down the POLITICO Pub
item.description: We swilled pints and grilled Labour politicians — from Ed Miliband to Bridget Phillipson — so you didn’t have to.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Northern Ireland leader accused of joining ‘mob’ to block Protestant parade
item.description: Unionists demand criminal consequences for First Minister Michelle O’Neill of Sinn Féin — who joined the road blockade against the Orange Order — as Northern Ireland’s government threatens to unravel.

item.title: [Politico Europe] UK Treasury minister says her old job as City of London rep is ‘not a conflict’
item.description: The City of London is lobbying hard against the prospect of a windfall tax on the banks ahead of the October budget.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Qu’est-ce qui peut encore arrêter le RN ?
item.description: Intentions de votes à la présidentielle, résultats aux sénatoriales, enlisement du bloc central : tout semble rouler pour Marine Le Pen. Mais tous les voyants sont-ils réellement au vert à sept mois du premier tour ? Comment faut-il analyser la contre-offensive de Jordan Bardella et de sa compagne dans la presse ce week-end ? Anthony […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Florida seeks injunction to hamper OpenAI development
item.description: Uthmeier cited newly disclosed breaches of U.S. and Australian government websites, along with reports of OpenAI agents going rogue.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Labour shouldn’t work with nationalists who want to break up the UK, says Welsh secretary
item.description: Stephen Kinnock says Plaid Cymru's support for independence would make a future coalition untenable.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Made in everywhere’: MEPs clash over reach of EU industrial law
item.description: Lead MEPs want 'Made in Europe' perks limited to the 27 member states. The centre-right, whose votes could decide the file, is split.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ukraine regains territory and captures POWs in frontline push
item.description: Operation Vivaldi has seen Ukraine make progress against Russian forces, which had been threatening a key fortress city.

item.title: [Financial Times] Erdoğan holds rare meeting with Germany’s potential next leader
item.description: Hendrik Wüst, premier of Germany’s most populous state, meets Turkish president on three-day visit amid speculation he could become chancellor

item.title: [EU Observer] Kallas regrets EU delisting of oligarchs, as Russia ‘ridicules’ Germany after UN meeting
item.description: Swedish defence minister Pål Jonson also said on Monday: "We should increase the price for Russian aggression, and it is only then that Russia will understand that they will not win this war".

item.title: [EU Observer] Munich talks keep EU return‑hub plan alive despite drop in border arrivals and budget questions
item.description: Irregular arrivals to the EU are falling, but the infrastructure of its militarised borders is only getting started. Interior ministers from various member states met in Munich to advance plans to offshore migration processing to third countries.

item.title: [DW] Sicily: Mount Etna ash disrupts Catania flights again
item.description: A thick ash cloud from Mount Etna has been disrupting flights to Catania in Sicily for several days. Italy and Europe's most active volcano, Etna has impacted air travel several times this summer.

item.title: [DW] Turkey: Comedian convicted for 'insulting' Erdogan in show
item.description: Deniz Goktas was convicted of two of three charges, including "insulting" the president, but was released pending the appeal process. Nominally, Turkey is a secular country with free speech.

item.title: [EU Observer] Protesters in Brussels press EU on ‘broken promises’ over caged animals
item.description: Animal rights activists call for the commission to finally table cage ban proposals after years of delays, while Irish Ferries has 15 days to respond to a new complaint about transporting calves without giving them food.

item.title: [EU Observer] Baltic states seek to calm panic on Russia, in role reversal
item.description: Warnings about Russia's escalation against Nato have prompted fear in Europe, but the Baltic states' risk assessments remain unchanged.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukrainians captured 250 Russian soldiers during Operation Vivaldi (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,677)
item.description: Telegram channels and satellite images reveal a quieter truth behind official statements: Russian lines north of Sloviansk are buckling, logistics hubs are burning, and both sides are scrambling to adapt to a war increasingly fought by drones.

item.title: [Financial Times] Nvidia launches record $150bn share buyback
item.description: Chipmaker’s plan to repurchase stock comes as share price gains have slowed this year

item.title: [Financial Times] Why Europe’s centre will hold
item.description: The 1930s are not a good guide to the politics of the 21st century

item.title: [EU Observer] What the new De Gaulle film leaves out on how WWII ended for eastern Europe
item.description: While European cinemas cheer de Gaulle’s triumphant return to Paris, Polish, Czech, and Baltic leaders endured far longer, lonelier fights for freedom that Washington, Moscow, and even Paris preferred to forget.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: How are Europeans contributing to the reconstruction of Gaza?
item.description: Rebuilding Gaza will require tens of billions of dollars, and the 883.6m package announced by the EU is not nearly enough.

item.title: [EU Observer] Volkswagen benefited from €1.5bn in German EV subsidies as it lobbies EU to hit Chinese cars harder
item.description: The EU imposed tariffs on Chinese electric cars in 2024. Today, Beijing's hybrid cars are making record sales in Europe amid fresh German calls to extend the tariffs.

item.title: [Financial Times] The crisis at Big Law powerhouse Weil
item.description: One of America’s most prestigious firms is in turmoil as a series of departures prompts talk of a merger

item.title: [EU Observer] THIS WEEK: Interior ministers discuss Fortress Europe, as Kallas goes to Syria
item.description: Interior ministers will discuss how to secure borders and deport more immigrants in the wake of the Ceuta episode, while foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas takes EU diplomacy to Syria.

item.title: [DW] 'Lithuanian skies are NATO skies': DW speaks with Lithuanian premier Mindaugas Sinkevicius
item.description: In a DW interview, Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius discussed threats to Lithuania from Russia and Belarus, NATO's need for stronger air defense and why military spending alone cannot ensure security.

item.title: [EU Observer] First blind the Russians, then catch them with robots: Ukraine’s Operation Vivaldi shows cutting edge of modern warfare (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,674)
item.description: By driving Russian forces back to their 2022 lines and crippling refineries deep in Samara, Operation Vivaldi shows how a tech-heavy Ukrainian corps can threaten not just a single sector near Lyman, but Russia’s wider ability to wage war.

item.title: [DW] How Bulgaria become a global leader in battery storage and what this means for the country's grid and energy market?
item.description: In under two years, Bulgaria has become one of the world's most battery-intensive energy markets. Can the surge last — and what will it mean for conventional power generators?

item.title: [DW] Italy to ban burqa in schools, limit foreign pupils
item.description: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s government has passed new school rules capping the number of students who don't speak fluent Italian and banning face coverings.
